segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he showed me a river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing out from the throne of God and of the Lamb

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: through the middle of the city’s main street. On either side of the river stood the tree of life, producing twelve crops of fruit, yielding its fruit every month, and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There will no longer be anything accursed. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in the city, and his slaves will serve him;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: they will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there will be no more night; they have no need of the light of a lamp or the light of the sun, because the Lord God will shine on them, and they will reign forever and ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “These words are faithful and true, and the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, sent his angel to show his slaves what must happen soon.”

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “And look, I am coming soon! Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I had heard and seen them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who was showing them to me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Don’t do that! I am a fellow slave with you and your brothers the prophets and those who keep the words of this book. Worship God!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to me,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: Let the one who does wrong still do wrong, and the filthy still be filthy; let the righteous still do righteousness, and the holy still be holy.”

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look, I am coming soon, and my reward is with me, to repay each person according to their work.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they will have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by the gates.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Outside are the dogs and the sorcerers and the sexually immoral and the murderers and the idolaters and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I, Jesus, sent my angel to testify to you about these things for the assemblies. I am the root and the descendant of David, the bright morning star.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Spirit and the bride say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Come!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And let the one who hears say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Come!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who wishes take the water of life as a gift.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to them, God will add to that person the plagues written in this book;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away that person’s share in the tree of life and in the holy city, which are written about in this book.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The one who testifies to these things says,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Yes, I am coming soon.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Amen! Come, Lord Jesus!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.

notes.phrase: through the middle of the city’s main street
notes.note: The Greek can be punctuated two ways. Taken with verse 1, as here and in the SBLGNT, the river flows down the middle of the street. Taken with what follows, the tree of life stands “in the middle of the street and on either side of the river.” Both readings are widely held.

The singular “tree” standing on both banks is probably collective, a line of trees, as in Ezekiel 47:12, where trees along the temple river bear fruit every month and have leaves for healing. The name recalls the tree in the garden of Genesis 2–3, from which humanity was barred. The vision shows access to it restored.

This is the same Greek word that is rendered “Gentiles” elsewhere in the New Testament, where it means the non-Jewish peoples. In Revelation the scope is the peoples of the whole world, so “nations” is used.

The Greek word is the ordinary term for a slave, someone who belongs to a master, and a first-century reader heard it that way. Most English versions soften it to “servants,” though some recent ones use “slaves.” In the Septuagint the word is also a title of honor for those who belong to God, such as Moses and the prophets. The related word in verse 9 is rendered “fellow slave.”

The Greek does not mark a change of speaker from the angel of verse 6, but “I am coming soon” can only be Jesus’s own announcement (compare verses 12 and 20). It is treated here as his voice breaking in; others take the angel to be speaking in his name. Voices shift without notice throughout this closing section, and the assignment of verses 14–15 and 17 is likewise a judgment call.

Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read “those who do his commandments.” The two phrases look and sound alike in Greek. The earliest witnesses support “wash their robes,” which echoes 7:14, and modern editions adopt it.

Dogs were mostly scavengers, not pets, and “dog” was a common term of contempt for the unclean or shameless. In Deuteronomy 23:18 it appears to refer to a male cult prostitute, and some see that sense here. More likely it is a general label for the morally impure, heading the list that follows.

The Greek word meant a gathering of people. It was the term for a city’s civic assembly and, in the Septuagint, for Israel assembled before God. “Church” is the near-universal rendering and is not wrong, but it now suggests a building or an institution. Here the word refers to the seven communities addressed in chapters 1–3.

The speaker of verses 18–19 is uncertain. Verse 20 calls Jesus “the one who testifies to these things,” which suggests the warning is his, and a number of scholars read it so. Many others take it as John’s own solemn conclusion, and it is printed here in the author’s voice. The warning is modeled on Deuteronomy 4:2 and 12:32, which forbid adding to or taking from God’s commands.

The King James Version reads “book of life.” That reading has almost no Greek manuscript support. It arose in the Latin tradition, where the words for “book” and “tree” differ by two letters. It entered the early printed Greek text because Erasmus lacked a Greek manuscript for the final verses and translated them back from Latin.

This is the Greek equivalent of the Aramaic prayer Marana tha, “Our Lord, come!”, which Paul quotes untranslated in 1 Corinthians 16:22. It was evidently a fixed cry in the worship of the earliest Aramaic-speaking believers.

The manuscripts end the book in several ways: “with all,” “with the holy ones,” “with all the holy ones,” and “with you all,” and many add “Amen.” The SBLGNT prints the shortest form, on the view that the others are scribal expansions. The matter is not settled.

candidates.reason: “Slave” versus “servant” (and σύνδουλος as “fellow slave”) recurs across every book, and translators divide on it, so it needs one decision.
ταχύ and ἐν τάχει can be “soon” or “quickly,” and the choice affects how Revelation’s expectation is read from 1:1 to 22:20.
The plural for fellow believers is rendered “brothers,” “brothers and sisters,” or “fellow believers” by different translators and should be uniform.
The πορν- word group recurs in vice lists across the New Testament, with renderings ranging from “fornicators” to “the sexually immoral” to “whoremongers.”
The attention particle is very frequent, and “behold,” “look,” “see,” or omission should be settled once for the whole translation.
